EDS AI Workflow (Eitri Agentic Dev Workflow)

Skills catalogue

This catalogue lists the skills in the EDS AI Workflow (Eitri) and the Matt Pocock base set it builds on: what each does, who maintains it and whether it is available. Use it to look up a skill named on the other pages.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions that an AI agent runs for one task. Two guide skills help a team find the right one: /ask-workflow covers the PO/BA and developer harnesses, and /ask-matt covers Matt Pocock’s skills.

Read the catalogue

Each table names the skill, who maintains it, its status and what it does. Maintained by identifies the skill’s maintainer: “CoreX EDS team” marks an EDS add-on skill. Where a skill wraps a tool from outside EDS, the tool is linked. Step and gate numbers refer to the Developer harness page.

Labels on this page

Available
Ready to use.
Planned
In development and not yet available. Do not count on it as a control.

AIHow AI can help

Choose a skill by the result you need

A skill gives an agent a reusable procedure for a bounded task. Use the catalogue to connect that task to its inputs, resulting artefact and next reviewer.

Give AI
The task, required input artefacts, relevant context and the selected skill’s instructions.
AI helps by
Following the selected planning, implementation or review procedure and producing its documented artefacts or findings.
People check
Check that the skill applies to the task and is available in the installed workflow. Compare its result with the original requirement and reproduce relevant checks.
Keep as evidence
The selected skill and version, inputs, output artefacts, check results and unresolved findings.

Matt Pocock’s skills

The documented setup installs these base skills from Matt Pocock’s public skill set. Record the installed revision: upstream names and behaviour can change. The descriptions say how this workflow uses them.

Matt Pocock’s skills used in the workflow
SkillStatusWhat it does
/ask-mattAvailableAn interactive guide to Matt Pocock’s engineering skills.
/setup-matt-pocock-skillsAvailableConfigures the repository’s issue tracker, triage labels and domain-document layout. Step 1.
/wayfinderAvailablePlans work too large for one agent session as a shared map of investigation tickets, resolved one at a time. PO/BA Path 2 and Step 5.
/grill-with-docsAvailableStress-tests the plan for a well-defined story against the domain model and records what is agreed. Step 5.
/grill-meAvailableQuestions the author about an artefact until it matches their intent. Optional during planning and at both human gates.
/grillingAvailableQuestions a plan or design thoroughly before building. Used by /wayfinder.
/domain-modelingAvailableBuilds the project’s domain model and shared language, and records architecture decisions.
/codebase-designAvailableSupplies shared vocabulary for designing modules with small interfaces that are easy to test.
/prototypeAvailableBuilds a throwaway prototype to answer a design question.
/to-specAvailableTurns the decisions reached into a specification and publishes it to the tracker. Produces the TRD in Step 6.
/to-ticketsAvailableBreaks a specification into tracer-bullet issues with declared dependencies. Step 9.
/improve-codebase-architectureAvailableFinds modules worth deepening and presents the options in a report. Step 13.
/code-reviewAvailableReviews a change against coding standards and against the specification, in two independent reviews. Step 15 and Gate 2.
/diagnosing-bugsAvailableA structured diagnosis method for hard bugs and performance regressions. Step 16.

Frontend quality

The Impeccable suite by Paul Bakaus covers frontend quality in three layers.

Impeccable frontend quality commands
CommandWhen to useWhat it covers
/impeccable auditAfter implementing an interface sliceAccessibility, performance, theming, responsive design and common anti-patterns in generated code.
/impeccable hardenBefore shipping a featureResilience: edge cases, error and empty states, text overflow and slow networks.
/impeccable polishOn prototypes or before a stakeholder reviewVisual finish: alignment, typography, spacing, interaction states and copy.

Compliance

Compliance skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/policiesCoreX EDS teamAvailableHolds the organisational policy references and applies them to audit a document for security and governance compliance.
/spec-complianceCoreX EDS teamAvailableAudits a specification or TRD against the policy references. Step 8.
/issue-verificationCoreX EDS teamAvailableConfirms that each issue is a true tracer bullet and that the set is consistent, before publishing. Step 10.

The documented Eitri policy pack contains two reference checklists: IM8 application security checks (36 packaged checks) and the ARC agentic AI governance checks (88 packaged checks). Read how a team adds its own.

Implementation

/do-work runs the build loop. /code-reviewer is the quality and compliance gate inside that loop.

AIHow AI can help

A review skill can flag missing requirements or coding-standard violations in a supplied change. Give it the original issue or TRD and applicable rules. Reviewers inspect the cited code and reproduce findings; retain confirmed issues and reasons for dismissing unsupported findings before the next decision.

Architecture linting

These skills turn architecture decisions into runnable boundary tests, so violations fail the build. They use ArchUnit for a JVM backend and dependency-cruiser for a JavaScript or TypeScript frontend.

Architecture linting skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/arch-tests-planCoreX EDS teamAvailableAnalyses the project and writes a plan of the architecture rules to test. Step 4.
/arch-tests-genCoreX EDS team, wrapping ArchUnit and dependency-cruiserAvailableGenerates the boundary tests from the plan. Step 4.
/arch-tests-gen-featureCoreX EDS team, wrapping ArchUnit and dependency-cruiserAvailableGenerates boundary tests for one new feature. Step 14.

MCP integrations

Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations connect the agent to library documentation, coding guidelines and other sources of project context.

Model Context Protocol integrations
IntegrationMaintained byStatusWhat it does
Context7UpstashPlannedLive, version-specific library documentation, fetched when the agent needs to confirm how a library behaves. Step 3.
Sonar Context AugmentationSonarPlannedCoding guidelines, architectural awareness and code search, for the Sonar review and the build loop.

Path to production

These skills run before a release is promoted. /pre-prod-check runs them all in sequence; each can also be run alone. See when each runs.

Path to production skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/pre-prod-checkCoreX EDS teamAvailableRuns the seven readiness gates in sequence, then writes a consolidated sign-off report for the Tech Lead.
/gen-code-docsCoreX EDS teamAvailableGenerates API documentation from comments in the code.
/gen-auth-matrixCoreX EDS teamAvailableGenerates an authorisation matrix showing which roles can reach which endpoints.
/tech-arch-docCoreX EDS teamAvailableScans every module and generates a technical architecture document.
/dependency-vuln-scanCoreX EDS teamAvailableScans dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and produces a point-in-time report.

Sources

References last checked: 9 November 2026.

  1. CoreX EDS team. Eitri skills catalogue (skills-catalogue.md), internal revision not supplied. Primary source for skill groups, maintainers, descriptions and Available/Planned labels; the editorial review records the two grilling skills used by the workflow but absent from the supplied catalogue. The internal document and revision are unavailable here; the workflow owner must confirm the installed controls, availability and enforcement. The reference-check date does not verify that implementation. Used in catalogue conventions, skill groups, base-skill uses, additional skills.
  2. CoreX EDS team. Eitri harness workflow — README, sections 2–4; internal revision not supplied. Primary workflow source; the editorial review gives this README priority over the older operating handbook. The internal document and revision are unavailable here; the workflow owner must confirm the installed controls, availability and enforcement. The reference-check date does not verify that implementation. Used in planning, build-loop adaptations, reviews, release gates.
  3. SG Tech Stack. Eitri AI coding workflow — self-paced training. Live, version-dependent public training, not certification of an installed harness. Its five-phase view and /dependency-orchestrator differ from the local 19-step view and /project-horizon; do not silently substitute one revision for the other. The Eitri skills lesson records the documented defaults and policy-pack counts. Used in the 36/88 packaged-check split.
  4. Matt Pocock. Engineering skills — upstream skill set, live repository; installed revision not identified. Underlying investigation, specification, slicing, implementation and review skills; the descriptions on this page explain their use or adaptation in the documented EDS workflow, not a guarantee of current upstream names or behaviour. Used in base skills, the /do-work adaptation of /implement, the /fry-me adaptation.
  5. Paul Bakaus. Impeccable — frontend quality skills. Underlying audit, harden and polish suite. The catalogue describes the documented workflow use; confirm the installed revision and host invocation. Used in frontend audit, harden and polish.
  6. Singapore Government. Instruction Manual 8 (IM8) — ICT and Smart Systems policy framework. Policy reference, not evidence of the installed application-security checklist or its enforcement. Packaged checks are a scoped selection, not a total for the entire framework; confirm the applicable policy and policy-pack versions with their owners. Used in packaged application-security checks, code review.
  7. GovTech. Agentic Risk & Capability Framework (ARC). Governance framework underlying the documented TRD audit. Checklist coverage and applicable versions require owner confirmation; a document assessment does not establish executable or runtime enforcement. Used in packaged agentic-governance checks.
  8. PIT project. PIT — Java mutation testing. Underlying mutation-testing tool; the documented 70% harness default is configurable, not a requirement established by this tool reference. Used in mutation testing.
  9. Stryker Mutator project. StrykerJS — JavaScript and TypeScript mutation testing. Underlying mutation-testing tool; the documented harness threshold and changed-file scope require the installed configuration. Used in mutation testing.
  10. Vercel. agent-browser — browser automation for agents. Underlying tool for acceptance checks and screenshots; its public documentation does not verify the EDS wrapper, test coverage or evidence. Used in browser testing.
  11. Microsoft. Playwright — end-to-end browser testing. Underlying test framework; the EDS campaign, verifier and repeat-run behaviour are local workflow conventions, not guarantees from this reference. Used in end-to-end testing.
  12. Semgrep. Semgrep — static security analysis. Underlying scanner reference, not verification of the rules, severity mapping or blocking behaviour configured in the EDS harness. Used in static analysis.
  13. Cursor. Thermo-nuclear code quality review — skill instructions. Live main-branch skill reference for maintainability review. The EDS wrapper and installed upstream revision require confirmation; review findings are not proof of correctness. Used in maintainability review.
  14. Sonar. Sonar — code quality and context augmentation. Product reference for the planned integration, not evidence that the EDS Sonar review or context augmentation is installed or enforced. Used in planned Sonar review, planned context augmentation.
  15. ArchUnit project. ArchUnit — Java architecture tests. Underlying architecture-test tool; the project reference does not verify the generated EDS tests or their enforcement. Used in architecture linting.
  16. Sander Verweij. dependency-cruiser — dependency rules for JavaScript and TypeScript. Live main-branch reference for architecture boundary checks; pin the version used by the repository. Used in architecture linting.
  17. Upstash. Context7 — version-specific library documentation. Tool reference for the planned documentation integration; a public product page does not establish its installation or availability in Eitri. Used in planned library documentation.
  18. OWASP. Threat Dragon — threat modelling. Underlying tool for data-flow diagrams and threat-model artefacts. Generated models still need review; the tool reference does not establish EDS readiness gates. Used in threat modelling.
